security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU advertises Zvknhb in the ISA string or device tree to the guest without also asserting Zvknha, or the TCG backend implements vsha2* with SEW=64 support but fails to support SEW=32, violating the implication that Zvknhb includes Zvknha's full SEW=32 functionality.
security_spec.summary: Zvknhb implies Zvknha: QEMU must enforce that enabling Zvknhb automatically enables Zvknha, otherwise guest software checking Zvknha on a Zvknhb-advertised machine will see missing SHA-256 SEW=32 acceleration and may fall back to software paths or trap on reserved SEW encodings, breaking guest crypto stack availability assumptions.

findings.finding: The ZVKNHB_IMPLIED rule does not include Zvknha in its implied_multi_exts array. Per the RISC-V Vector Crypto spec (zvk.adoc:483), 'Zvknhb implies Zvknha', meaning enabling Zvknhb must automatically enable Zvknha. Without this entry, a user can configure '-cpu rv64,zvknhb=true,zvknha=false' and QEMU will advertise Zvknhb in the ISA string/DTB without Zvknha, violating the spec-mandated dependency.

The validation function checks that Zvknhb requires Zve64x but does not validate that Zvknha is also enabled when Zvknhb is set. While the implied-rules engine should handle this, there is no hard validation to catch the case where a user explicitly disables Zvknha while enabling Zvknhb. This is a secondary defense gap — the implied-rules fix (finding above) is the primary fix needed.

The SEW check correctly implements the Zvknhb-includes-Zvknha semantics at the instruction translation level: vsha2* instructions accept SEW=32 when either Zvknha or Zvknhb is enabled, and additionally accept SEW=64 only when Zvknhb is enabled. This means the TCG decode path already handles the implication correctly for instruction execution, even though the ISA string advertising does not.
